title: What If Everyone Got a Superpower Except You?

facts.claim: In a 2011 Marist poll, mind reading and time travel tied as Americans' top superpower picks at 28% each; flying got 16%
facts.source: Marist Poll, Feb 2011 ('Holy Super Powers, Batman!'); reported by Time NewsFeed and The Daily Beast

facts.claim: Stanford psychiatrist David Spiegel estimates about one quarter of his patients cannot be hypnotized
facts.source: Stanford Medicine news, Oct 2012, 'Not getting sleepy?'; about 15% are highly hypnotizable

facts.claim: Average human visual reaction time is about a quarter of a second (median ~273 ms over millions of tests)
facts.source: Human Benchmark reaction time test statistics (humanbenchmark.com)

lines.text: At 9:41 a.m., your best friend starts floating in math class.
Bro! Bro! I'm flying!
Two feet off the ground. And around the room, everyone is lighting up. Your teacher reads minds. The girl behind you turns invisible. Then visible. Then invisible again.
You wait. And wait. Nothing happens.
Is it... loading?
8 billion people just got a superpower. Except you. And in 27 days, you'll be the only thing standing between one kid and every mind in the city.
In the next 30 days, you'll get kicked out of a casino, go viral with 12 million views, and stop a kid who can control every mind in the city. Every mind except one.
Here's how it works. Everyone got exactly one power. Random. You can't choose it. You can't trade it.
A 2011 Marist poll asked Americans which power they'd pick. Mind reading and time travel tied at 28 percent. Flying got 16.
Theo got flying. Two feet. Maximum.
It's still flying!
Your mom can heal any cut in 3 seconds. Your dad can talk to pigeons. The pigeons are not nice.
Honey, they called me bald.
And one kid in your class, Max, never told anyone what power he got. Remember Max.
The government sets up a hotline. Some powers arrive late, it says. Up to 30 days. So you start counting.
School becomes a disaster. The quarterback runs 90 miles an hour. Gym class is no longer fair.
The average person reacts in about a quarter of a second, according to millions of tests on Human Benchmark. The kid with super speed reacts before you finish blinking.
A boy in the hallway can talk to plants. He won't stop. The plants want him to stop.
And every single person asks you the same question.
So what's your power?
So what's your power?
Nobody gets nothing. You're hiding something.
Day 3. Your teacher tries to read your mind before a pop quiz.
Huh. Nothing. Is anyone in there?
At lunch, Theo high-fives you. And for one second, he drops out of the air like a rock.
Bro, what was that?
That's when you get it. You didn't get a power. You're the only person on Earth that powers don't work on. Good ones, bad ones, all of them. And if you touch someone, theirs switches off.
That's not as made up as it sounds. Stanford psychiatrist David Spiegel estimates about 1 in 4 of his patients can't be hypnotized at all.
Day 6. Every YouTuber on Earth uploads the same video. I tried every superpower for 24 hours.
Theo uploads Flying for 24 hours, 2 feet. It gets 40 views. 39 are his mom.
Then you upload yours. Testing every superpower on the one person it doesn't work on.
A mind reader reads nothing. A lie detector beeps at everything. A guy who freezes people freezes himself by accident.
12 million views in 3 days. Your mom heals your paper cut from opening the fan mail. Or tries to.
Why isn't it working? Sweetie, hold still!
Even your dad starts a channel. Pigeon Translations. It gets more views than Theo's.
How?!
Day 9. Casinos hire mind readers to catch cheaters at the poker table. They can read every player's cards. Except yours.
You win 14 hands in a row.
You. Need to leave. Now.
You get walked out by a guard who can walk through walls. He uses the door. Out of respect.
But being the only normal person gets weird.
The school trip to Paris takes 4 seconds. A teleporter takes the whole class. Except you, because teleporting doesn't work on you. You take the bus. It's a 9 hour bus ride to the airport.
Theo's flying club meets 2 feet off the ground. You sit on the floor.
You can hold my ankle. Wait, no, then I fall.
The only other person who never uses a power is Max. He sits alone at lunch. You never ask why. Nobody does.
Day 26. The hotline stops answering. 30 days is almost up. Still nothing.
Day 27. 3:15 p.m. The school speakers crackle. And Max finally uses his power.
Everyone. Stop.
And everyone stops. Mid step. Mid sentence. Mind control. Every person who can hear his voice does exactly what he says.
Now give me your phones.
1,200 students hand over their phones. Except you.
And it's spreading. His voice is on the city's emergency radio now. By midnight, every speaker in the state.
You call home. Your mom picks up. In the middle of a sentence, her voice goes flat.
Give him your phone, sweetie.
The clock says 3:22 p.m. 8 hours and 38 minutes until the whole state can hear him.
Give him your phone, bro.
Theo floats toward you. Two feet off the ground. Eyes completely blank.
You run for the radio room. Max tells the hallway to stop you.
The teleporter blinks in front of you. Nothing happens to you. A force field goes up. You walk straight through it. The freezer kid freezes. Himself. Again.
Stop. Stop! I said stop!
It doesn't work. It never did.
You don't fight him. You just grab his hand. And his power switches off. For everyone. All at once.
Across the city, 2 million people blink and wonder why they're holding someone else's phone.
I just wanted everybody to stop talking about their powers.
Yeah. Honestly? Same.
The police arrive 40 minutes later. Which means you hold hands with a supervillain for 40 minutes.
Max gets the only sentence that makes sense. He has to sit next to you. Every day. Until graduation.
Your dad's pigeons explain to him exactly what happened. In detail. They are still not nice.
Okay. You weren't hiding anything. And it was the best power in the building.
And Theo? He trips on the stairs. And floats. Two feet. Exactly enough not to hit the floor.
Still flying!
That night, at exactly 9:41, your phone buzzes. A message from an unknown number.
Your power is ready. Are you?
So if everyone got a superpower except you, what would you want yours to be? Tell us in the comments.
